title: Differing Bits Between Two Numbers
statement: Given two non-negative integers x and y, write both in binary and line them up from the lowest bit. Return the number of bit positions where they differ.

examples.why: 5 is 101 and 3 is 011. They differ in the two highest of the three positions.
y is 31 ones in a row and x has no set bits at all.

hints: Is there a single operation that marks exactly the positions where two bits differ?
x XOR y has a 1 wherever the bits of x and y differ. Now count the 1s.
Counting: shift right and test the lowest bit, or repeatedly clear the lowest set bit with v & (v − 1).

explain.intuition:
XOR gives 1 for different bits and 0 for equal bits, so x ^ y turns the question into "how many 1 bits does this number have?"

For counting, the trick v & (v − 1) clears the lowest set bit: subtracting 1 flips that bit and every 0 below it, and the AND wipes them all. Repeating it until v is 0 loops once per set bit, not once per bit position.
steps: While v is not 0: set v = v & (v − 1) and add 1 to count.
pitfalls: Comparing the decimal digits or the lengths of the binary strings instead of lining the bits up from the lowest end.
In JavaScript, shifting with >> on a value whose top bit is set keeps the sign and loops forever. Use >>> for an unsigned shift.

solutions.title: XOR and check every bit
solutions.idea: Take x XOR y and look at its lowest bit 31 times, shifting right each time.

solutions.title: XOR and clear the lowest set bit
solutions.idea: v & (v − 1) removes one set bit per step, so the loop runs once per differing position.

followups: Return the sum of differing bits over every pair in an array of n numbers, faster than O(n²).
Count set bits for every number from 0 to n in O(n) total.
